description: anyone can bake ep. 1: 🍪 Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies 🍪 simple, iconic, deeply comforting, and my favorite (and most popular) recipe of all time. I’m sharing my go-to tips and tricks for nailing that perfect chewy center, crisp edge, showstopper cookie every. single. time. the full recipe is linked in my bio and also on bromabakery.com!
transcript: Welcome to Anyone Can Bake, the series where I show you how to make classic baking recipes in a way that actually feels doable. We're kicking things off with my most popular recipe of all time, my brown butter chocolate chip cookies. They get over 500,000 pages a month on my blog, have been made by literally millions of people, and are in my opinion, the best cookies of all time. So let's get into exactly how to make them. Start out by browning three quarters of a cup of butter on the stove over low heat. Any higher at new risk cooking off too much water and burning the butter. Stir every 15 seconds or so until you see small brown flecks in the bottom of your pan. As soon as they're light golden brown, take the pan off the heat and let it rest until it's warm but not hot to the touch, which should be about five minutes. Next, measure out your brown sugar. Brown sugar should always be packed before it's measured, so push it against the side of the bag before using the back of a butter knife to level it off, getting the most accurate measurement. Then pour the warm brown butter into a mixing bowl along with the packed brown sugar, some granulated sugar, and an entire tablespoon of vanilla extract. It sounds like a lot but it adds so much depth to these cookies and really enhances the warmth of the other ingredients. Mix until just combined, then add in a large egg along with an extra egg yolk, which really enhances the richness in the dough. Next, flour. Measuring this accurately is so important because overmeasuring your flour can lead to dry and puffy cookies. For that reason, I like to use a scaled away my flour, but if you don't have a scale, you can use the fluff and scoop method. Use a large spoon to fluff up your flour in the bag, then scoop it into the measuring cup before leveling it off with a butter knife. It's slightly annoying, but it does lead to the most accurate measurement. Add that to your bowl along with a little baking soda and use a spatula to fold everything together by hand until just combined. Mixing any more will make your dough tougher and tighter, and we want this nice soft dough. Last, chocolate. You can really use whatever you have on hand. Mini chips, chocolate bars, but my favorite are chocolate disks. They're thin and wide, melt beautifully, and leave you with big pools of chocolate throughout your cookies. Then it's time to roll your dough. I strongly recommend using a cookie scoop, then rolling the dough into balls in your hands to smooth the edges. And last pro tip, I like to move some of the chocolate pieces to the top of my cookies so that you see them when they bake. Cover the dough and let it chill in the fridge for at least one hour, but up to overnight. Again, it's annoying, but letting the rest is instrumental to developing maximum flavor and texture. When you're ready, let the dough balls come to room temperature, then bake them on a light colored cookie sheet at 350 degrees for 12 to 13 minutes. To tell if they're perfectly cooked, touch the middle. It should be a little bit spongy while the outside should be hard. Then let them cool completely on the pan. They'll continue to cook as they cool and set into the perfect gooey texture. So there you have it, my absolutely perfect brown butter chocolate chip cookies. They're crispy on the outside, soft and chewy on the inside, and have a warm, rich brown butter flavor and gooey texture. The recipe is also linked in my profile and searchable on Bromabakeri.com. Happy baking!
